historical_cashout_count.calculation_time: Count of cashouts with cashout_occurred_at <= t_complaint

account_risk_score.calculation_time: Deterministic heuristic computed from estimated_remaining and delay_minutes

minutes_since_last_transaction.calculation_time: Derived from max(completed_at) of past transactions (completed_at <= t_complaint)

model_b_location_ranking.synthetic_artifact_explanation: The Random Forest ranker achieves 95.81% Top-1 (vs 71.73% for Distance baseline) because of a synthetic candidate injection artifact. In the dataset generator, candidate sets are generated by selecting the 7 nearest ATMs to the account. When a ground-truth cashout occurs at a distant ATM (e.g. >50 km), the generator forces candidate coverage by replacing candidate #7 with that distant ATM. As a result, 23.53% of targets (457 cases) have distance > 50 km, whereas only 0.5% of non-targets (58 candidates) have distance > 50 km. The probability that a candidate with distance > 50 km is the ground truth target is 88.74%. The non-linear Random Forest learns this bimodal distribution (assigning high rank to distance==0 km AND distance>50 km), while linear models and simple distance ranking rank distant ATMs last.
model_b_location_ranking.recommended_fix: Generate candidate sets using realistic geo-radius / cluster-based candidate generators without distant-target injection.

model_c_timing_regressor.target_definition: Remaining minutes from prediction_timestamp (t_complaint) to actual_next_cashout_at
model_c_timing_regressor.synthetic_generator_distribution: In networks.py (get_cashout_time), future cash-out occurrence times are generated via `mins_after_complaint = rng.randint(10, 180)`. Because this delay is drawn from a uniform distribution Uniform(10, 180) independent of the input features, the regression models achieve R^2 ~ 0.00 and MAE ~ 41.8 min (matching the theoretical expectation of (180-10)/4 = 42.5 min for a uniform random variable). The model is not defective; the underlying synthetic data generator lacks feature-correlated timing signal.
model_c_timing_regressor.recommended_action: In future synthetic data releases, introduce feature-dependent timing distributions (e.g. log-normal delay correlated with modus operandi, transaction velocity, and reporting latency).

safe_to_proceed: Model A: Future Cash-Out Occurrence Classifier (ROC-AUC 0.8617, PR-AUC 0.9569, Brier 0.1245). Point-in-time state verified, zero leakage.
requires_retraining_or_fix: Model B: Location Candidate Ranker (Random Forest reports 95.81% Top-1 due to synthetic candidate injection artifact; distance baseline of 71.73% is safer until candidate generator is updated).
Model C: Timing Regressor (Functional and leak-free, but R^2 ~ 0.00 due to uniform random delay in generator; median baseline is optimal for current synthetic data).
